title: Historical and contemporary units of measurement
notes: 'si' is the unit's value in the base unit for its category (m, m², L, kg, each). Convert any unit to any other in the same category via si: amount × from.si / to.si.
'definition' records how the unit is defined (a multiple of another unit, the square/cube of a length, or a base value), so relationships like '1 furlong = 10 chains' can be shown.

'precision': 'exact' = fixed by law/definition (e.g. 1 inch = 25.4 mm); 'approximate' = a well-measured historical standard; 'uncertain' = variable or reconstructed, with 'low'/'high' giving the plausible range across sources, periods or regions. Many pre-modern units varied from town to town.
'era' is [first, last] year of common use (approximate; negative = BCE; null = still in use).
Volume units carry subcategory 'liquid' or 'dry' where the distinction matters.
Units with 'fictional': true come from novels and films ('work' names the source); 'era' starts at publication, and 'precision' reflects how firmly the work fixes the value.
